problems.stem: To publish a user site at https://mlopez.github.io with GitHub Pages, what must the repository be named?
problems.explanation: A GitHub user site is served from a repository named exactly username.github.io. Any other repo name produces a project site at a /repo subpath instead.

problems.stem: Your home page is in a file called Index.HTML. The published site shows a 404 at the root URL. What is the most likely cause?
options: GitHub Pages requires the entry file to be named index.html in lowercase
GitHub Pages does not support HTML files
You need to pay for hosting
problems.explanation: GitHub Pages serves index.html (lowercase) as the root document. Index.HTML is treated as a different filename, so the root URL has nothing to serve.

problems.stem: An AI assistant tells you to run 'git push -f origin main' to fix a rejected push on your shared class repo. What is the responsible move?
options: Run it immediately; force-push always fixes push errors
Pause: a force push can overwrite teammates' commits, so first run 'git pull' to integrate their work, then push normally
Delete the repository and start over
Ignore the error and keep editing files locally forever
problems.explanation: Force-pushing to a shared branch can erase others' commits. AI suggestions about destructive git commands must be judged against the cost; pulling first is the safe path.

problems.stem: You accidentally committed a file named secrets.txt containing an API key. What should you do?
options: Nothing; private repos can never leak
Remove the file, add it to .gitignore, commit the removal, and rotate (regenerate) the exposed key
Rename the file to notes.txt and leave the key in it
Make the repo public so more people can help
problems.explanation: Once a key is committed it is in history. You remove and gitignore the file and, crucially, rotate the key, because the old one must be treated as compromised.
